title: Scaling NVIDIA TensorRT Performance Optimization Beyond a Single Build Route with the Global Performance Tuner, Part 2 | NVIDIA Technical Blog
gist: Part 2 of NVIDIA's series describes how the TensorRT 11.1 Global Performance Tuner works. It represents scheduling alternatives as build routes made of more than 200 compiler knobs, exposed through C++ APIs and a trtexec tuning loop that rejects routes that crash or fail accuracy and keeps the fastest. Across ten workloads, tuning gave end-to-end speedups of 1.14x to 1.63x over the default route. A Python version is planned for Torch-TensorRT 2.15.

insights.claim: Across ten evaluated workloads, the TensorRT Global Performance Tuner delivered end-to-end inference speedups of 1.14x to 1.63x over the default TensorRT build route.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Gains of 14-63% from software alone effectively raise the inference capacity of installed NVIDIA GPUs and reinforce the CUDA/TensorRT moat.

insights.claim: In the Global Performance Tuner, a build route is a concrete combination of compiler knob values, each knob having a finite set of allowed values and a default. TensorRT 11.1 exposes more than 200 tunable knobs.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: A large configuration space makes automated search, and therefore build-time GPU compute, central to deployment.
insights.quote: TensorRT 11.1 provides more than 200 knobs for tuning.

insights.claim: TensorRT exposes setBuildRoute, getBuildRoute and getAllBuildRoutes on IBuilderConfig so developers can apply, inspect and discover routes and build custom tuners. A Python implementation is planned for Torch-TensorRT 2.15.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Opening tuning APIs to PyTorch users extends NVIDIA's software lock-in into the dominant framework ecosystem.
insights.quote: The same implementation in Python will be released in Torch-TensorRT 2.15.

insights.claim: trtexec expands a regex-like route expression into concrete build routes, builds and measures each one, excludes routes that crash during building or fail accuracy during inference, and selects the engine with the best end-to-end performance.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: An open-source reference tuner lowers the cost for customers to adopt per-model optimization.
insights.quote: All build routes that crash during building or fail accuracy during inference are excluded from best-engine selection.

insights.claim: A knob combination specifies a build route but not the complete engine. TensorRT still performs tactic selection and may reconcile knob values with constraints imposed by the network.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: Tuning results are not fully deterministic configurations and must be revalidated.

insights.claim: The Global Performance Tuner treats accuracy as a constraint that filters candidates, backed by user-supplied metrics and golden datasets, and performance as the ranking criterion among eligible candidates. This makes the speed-accuracy trade-off a constrained-optimization problem.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: A systematic path to quantization can raise inference throughput without unacceptable quality loss, which matters for inference economics.

insights.claim: In a thought experiment with four binary Q/DQ quantization knobs, giving 16 candidates, full quantization is fastest but may fail accuracy. With epsilon at infinity, a performance-only optimizer could even pick a meaningless empty solution, so performance alone is not a sufficient objective.
insights.speaker: Jian Hu
insights.so_what: This shows why the accuracy threshold that users set is the key lever when automating reduced-precision deployment.
insights.quote: This limiting case demonstrates why performance alone is not a sufficient optimization objective.
